title: The Agent Native Company — Rick Blalock, Agentuity
talk_summary: Rick Blalock of Agentuity describes what an 'agent native' company looks like: AI agents embedded in product, operations, and culture, with humans acting as orchestrators/conductors rather than cogs. The talk is mostly cultural and organizational philosophy (hiring for AI fluency, flatter org charts, morning/afternoon agent-review rhythms) with almost no concrete technical mechanisms.

takeaways.what_they_do: Humans start the day by checking what agents did overnight and kicking off new work, then review outputs (PRs, collateral, emails) around lunchtime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the morning time is check out what agents did what they need to do kick off the things that they need to do and then come around I don't know around lunchtime review everything

takeaways.what_they_do: Each employee acts as lead/manager of their own agent counterparts, orchestrating swarms (e.g., content marketing) that execute async and hand back ready-to-go output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have content marketing swarms that we use multiple agents that that I'm orchestrating

takeaways.what_they_do: New hires spend their first weeks setting up their agent tooling/systems, with an engineer attached to ensure agents are running.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you probably would expect them the first few weeks to solely be focused on getting their agent set up to do their job

takeaways.technique: Self-learning agent that documents codebase conventions
takeaways.what_they_do: They use Cognition's Devin, which over months learned and documented how they handle things in their codebase, becoming a persistent knowledge asset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: now over time it's learned so much. It's documented so much of our code. It knows how we handle certain things
